title: Rotational Mechanics
standard_text: Rotational mechanics: angular displacement, velocity and acceleration; torque; moment of inertia; rotational equilibrium; angular momentum and its conservation; rolling motion. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Physics 1, Quarter 2)
meta_desc: Free Physics 1 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 2): torque, center of mass, moment of inertia, angular momentum and rolling. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Angular momentum is conserved when there is no external torque.
body_html:
How to think about it

Rotational motion is described by angular displacement (radians), angular velocity ω and angular acceleration α. A torque τ = rF sin θ causes angular acceleration; an object is in rotational equilibrium when the net torque is zero.

The moment of inertia I measures how hard it is to change an object's rotation; it depends on mass and how far the mass is from the axis. Angular momentum L = Iω is conserved when no external torque acts, which is why a spinning skater spins faster when pulling in her arms.

Example

A 20 N force acts 0.5 m from a hinge at 90°. Torque?

τ = rF

Answer: 10 N·m

Example

A diver tucks in. What happens to the spin rate?

I decreases, L constant

Answer: it increases

Common mistakes

  • Using the distance along the force instead of the perpendicular distance.
  • Thinking moment of inertia depends only on mass.
  • Mixing up angular and linear velocity units.

faq.q: Why is it easier to open a door by pushing far from the hinges?
faq.a: The larger lever arm gives more torque for the same force.

faq.q: Why does a rolling ball have extra kinetic energy?
faq.a: It has both translational and rotational kinetic energy.

A skater spinning at 4.00 rev/s pulls in her arms, so her moment of inertia becomes 1/2 of the value before. What is her new rate of spin?
items.e: Angular momentum is conserved: I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂, so ω₂ = 4.00 × 2 = 8.00 rev/s.

items.q: A skater spinning at 1.50 rev/s pulls in her arms, so her moment of inertia becomes 1/2.50 of the value before. What is her new rate of spin?
items.e: Angular momentum is conserved: I₁ω₁ = I₂ω₂, so ω₂ = 1.50 × 2.50 = 3.75 rev/s.
